text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- The leader of the liberal Free Democrats (FDP) threatens to end ruling coalition with Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) in row over policies of Finance Minister Theo Waigel.
- IG Metall trade union considers raising its pay claim for 1997.
- Government plans changes to law governing carmaker Volkswagen, reducing influence of state of Lower Saxony on the running of the company.
- Foreign investments by German companies are causing hardly any job losses at home, the Ifo economic institute says.
HANDELSBLATT
- Proposed "stability pact" for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) must have bite, finance ministry state secretary Juergen Stark says.
- Lower Saxony premier Gerhard Schroeder renews call for EMU to be postponed.
- Industrial production in western Germany should increase in final quarter of this year, Ifo survey predicts.
- Unions and employers in engineering sector no closer to finding compromise in dispute over sick pay.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- FDP rules out any further tax increases in the current legislative period.
- Schroeder's comments on EMU provoke sharp criticism from his fellow Social Democrats.
- Shorter working hours and lower taxes could halve German unemployement by the year 2000, an expert at the Federal Labour Office says.
- Foreign investment in Germany is declining while German investment abroad increases, Ifo institute says.
- Strong mark to blame for large portion of labour market problems, says Olaf Sievert, president of the central bank for Saxony and Thuringia.
DIE WELT
- German toxic waste transported illegally to Lebanon.
- Banks accuse finance officials of undermining confidentiality of bank customers in their search for tax evaders.
